Each original-pair projection of the restricted product measure is dominated by σ, so the averaged removal is dominated by σ. Each tuple has the same multiset of first coordinates and of second coordinates after permutation, so replacement preserves both marginals exactly.

The cost change is the integral of the positive improvement divided by k. Admissibility and ε-optimality bound it by ε. Setting ε=0 forces the improvement to be nonpositive almost everywhere for each given finite permutation.

For the median specialization the weighted finite cap cost is bounded Borel, and the near-optimality estimate applies to exactly the same coupling and cost. Every exchanged pair remains in the left/right legal product.
